video_title: Brothers in Arms, Partners in Healing: A Story about a Breakthrough in Treating Post-Traumatic...
gist: War on the Rocks interview with Navy flight surgeon turned Wave Neuroscience executive Eric Juan and Marine veteran Jeff Linquist on EEG-personalized transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) for PTSD. A seven-site sham-controlled trial reportedly showed a 52% symptom reduction and 68% remission (vs. 11-13% for SSRIs) and FDA clearance in 2026. The focus has moved to market access: VA/TRICARE/insurer coverage plus state-funded programs in Ohio, Florida and Missouri (~5,000 treated).

themes.theme: EEG-guided TMS clinical efficacy for PTSD

insights.claim: Wave Neuroscience's EEG-personalized TMS completed a seven-site, double-blind, randomized, sham-controlled FDA trial for PTSD that separated significantly from sham, and the FDA cleared it this year (2026) after a 2024 Breakthrough Device designation.
insights.speaker: Eric Juan (Wave Neuroscience)
insights.so_what: A new FDA-cleared device modality for PTSD creates a reimbursement and adoption catalyst for the company and the neuromodulation category.
insights.quote: It was a sevensite multi-center double blind randomized clinical control trial

insights.claim: The trial reported a 52% reduction in PTSD symptoms versus 11-13% for the only two FDA-approved PTSD drugs (sertraline/Zoloft and paroxetine), per the speaker's benchmark.
insights.speaker: Eric Juan (Wave Neuroscience)
insights.so_what: If replicated, a 4x efficacy gap vs. standard-of-care SSRIs threatens pharma incumbency in PTSD and supports premium device pricing.
insights.quote: our approach resulted in a 52% reduction in symptoms

insights.claim: The trial saw 68% remission, versus a VA study (researcher Brian Shiner) finding roughly 0% and 4.7% remission from pharmacotherapy for PTSD.
insights.speaker: Eric Juan (Wave Neuroscience)
insights.so_what: Remission, not just symptom reduction, is the payer-relevant endpoint; this gap is the core of the reimbursement pitch.
insights.quote: we saw 68% remission in in our clinical trial

insights.claim: Conventional (non-personalized) TMS trials for PTSD have repeatedly failed to separate from sham; the speaker claims this is the first TMS trial to achieve statistically significant separation, implying personalization is the moat.
insights.speaker: Eric Juan (Wave Neuroscience)
insights.so_what: Differentiation from commodity TMS clinics rests on the EEG-guided protocol, which matters for competitive positioning against established TMS device makers.
insights.quote: Ours is the first trial to separate significantly

insights.claim: Conventional TMS, FDA-cleared for depression for years, shows response rates around 50% (some studies 60-65%), which motivated EEG-based customization targeting disrupted neural connectivity.
insights.speaker: Eric Juan (Wave Neuroscience)
insights.so_what: Sets the baseline that personalized neuromodulation must beat to win share in the existing depression TMS market.

insights.claim: The company's chief scientific officer identified an EEG electrophysiologic biomarker present in the active-treatment group but not the sham group, correlated with symptom change, with publication pending under journal embargo.
insights.speaker: Eric Juan (Wave Neuroscience)
insights.so_what: An objective biomarker for PTSD response would be a major de-risking event for payers and a publication catalyst to watch.
insights.quote: she discovered what functionally is a biioarker

insights.claim: The trial took 7-8 years from phase 1 to submission, delayed by COVID and by expanding from two to seven sites to speed enrollment and improve generalizability.
insights.speaker: Eric Juan (Wave Neuroscience)
insights.so_what: Illustrates long timelines and capital needs for small neurotech device companies; site expansion is a trade-off between speed and data-integrity overhead.

insights.claim: EEG-based targeting uses a portable, suitcase-sized helmet unit producing a dynamic brain-network image in about 10-30 minutes, far cheaper and less labor-intensive than MRI-based targeting.
insights.speaker: Eric Juan (Wave Neuroscience)
insights.so_what: Low-capex, fast diagnostics enable scalable deployment in clinics, police and fire facilities, supporting unit economics.
insights.quote: an EEG is a very portable unit, smaller than a suitcase

insights.claim: Treatment uses a MagVenture figure-8, 1.8 Tesla coil over the medial prefrontal cortex delivering prescribed pulse trains to re-synchronize erratic neuron clusters.
insights.speaker: Eric Juan (Wave Neuroscience)
insights.so_what: Names the hardware supplier in the stack; growth of EEG-guided protocols could pull through coil/device demand.
insights.quote: we use a mag venture coil

insights.claim: Side effects are limited: 15-20% of patients get transient headaches; contraindications are mainly seizure history and intracranial metal, positioning it as a non-pharmaceutical option without liver toxicity, weight gain or hair loss.
insights.speaker: Eric Juan (Wave Neuroscience)
insights.so_what: A benign safety profile eases payer and clinician adoption versus psychiatric drugs.

insights.claim: Patients reportedly see rapid sleep improvement first, followed by behavior change; one patient slept through the night after the first session.
insights.speaker: Jeff Linquist (JLC Services)
insights.so_what: Fast, visible early responses support patient retention and word-of-mouth adoption.

themes.theme: Opioid reduction as a second-order benefit

insights.claim: A veteran patient on about 170 morphine-milligram equivalents per day (above 100 MME doubles annual all-cause mortality risk, per the physician) tapered to roughly 15-20 MME after treatment, without classic detox symptoms.
insights.speaker: Eric Juan (Wave Neuroscience)
insights.so_what: Positions the therapy within the opioid-crisis policy agenda, opening state funding channels beyond mental health budgets.
insights.quote: anything more than 100 morphine equivalents per day will will double your risk of all cause mortality

insights.claim: The patient attributes heavy opioid use mostly to emotional numbing rather than pain, implying PTSD treatment could reduce opioid demand in co-morbid veteran populations.
insights.speaker: Jeff Linquist (JLC Services)
insights.so_what: Cross-budget savings (opioid, hospitalization) strengthen the cost-effectiveness case to payers.

insights.claim: Both speakers stress the treatment works best stacked with counseling, EMDR and behavioral change rather than as a standalone cure.
insights.speaker: Jeff Linquist (JLC Services)
insights.so_what: Suggests bundled care models and partnerships with therapy providers rather than device-only revenue.
insights.quote: This is not a magic thing that makes everything in your life better

insights.claim: Ohio, Florida and Missouri fund EEG-guided TMS programs for veterans and first responders, together treating close to 5,000 patients since 2020 (about 4,000 in Ohio and Florida, about 1,000 in Missouri).
insights.speaker: Jeff Linquist (JLC Services)
insights.so_what: State legislation is a pre-reimbursement revenue channel and proof point while federal and commercial coverage is pending.

insights.claim: Ohio's program, pushed by former Navy SEAL state Senator Frank Hogan (as transcribed), created a bill template that other states can copy; the go-to-market plan is to find a legislative 'champion' in each state.
insights.speaker: Jeff Linquist (JLC Services)
insights.so_what: A replicable state-by-state legislative template points to a predictable, if slow, expansion path that investors can track by bill count.
insights.quote: now other states can plagiarize that bill if they want to

insights.claim: State programs publish real-time de-identified dashboards of patients treated and outcomes, which legislators use to justify spending to taxpayers.
insights.speaker: Eric Juan (Wave Neuroscience)
insights.so_what: Transparent outcomes data lowers political risk for renewals and makes expansion to new states easier.

insights.claim: Florida sheriffs, Miami fire and sheriff departments, the Police Benevolent Association, and Columbus FOP are pulling the technology into first-responder wellness programs.
insights.speaker: Jeff Linquist (JLC Services)
insights.so_what: Institutional demand from public-safety employers is a B2B channel separate from insurer reimbursement.

insights.claim: With scientific validation done, the main bottleneck is now market access: the company is lobbying the VA, TRICARE and commercial insurers for coverage decisions.
insights.speaker: Eric Juan (Wave Neuroscience)
insights.so_what: Coverage decisions from VA/TRICARE are the key catalysts that would turn FDA clearance into scaled revenue.
insights.quote: Now that we have that, it's about market access

insights.claim: The targeted US addressable population is about 13 million people diagnosed with PTSD, a disproportionate share being domestic-violence and sexual-trauma survivors, not just veterans.
insights.speaker: Eric Juan (Wave Neuroscience)
insights.so_what: The TAM extends well beyond the veteran niche, into mainstream commercial insurance.

insights.claim: Personalized EEG-guided TMS has treated roughly 40,000 patients cumulatively, versus millions of conventional TMS treatments for depression worldwide.
insights.speaker: Eric Juan (Wave Neuroscience)
insights.so_what: Still early penetration relative to the broader TMS installed base, so there is runway if reimbursement lands.

insights.claim: Despite FDA clearance and state programs, the speakers say the business is only in three states and has a long way to go.
insights.speaker: Jeff Linquist (JLC Services)
insights.so_what: Adoption is early; most upside depends on payer coverage and multi-state expansion, not current footprint.
insights.quote: We're only in three states, so have a long way to go
